findings.title: Nothing checks the dependencies for known vulnerabilities, and eighteen are present including two critical
findings.evidence: The same gap this project's dependency review found on ITEM-1, recorded again because the rule still does not hold at this commit rather than because the change caused it. pr-checks.yml runs verify, repo rules and secret scanning; peer-ai.yml runs peer-ai check. Searching .github for npm audit, osv-scanner, trivy, snyk or dependency-review-action returns nothing, and there is no dependabot.yml or renovate.json, so dependencies are checked neither on change nor on a schedule, and no time to fix is set. npm audit at this commit reports 18 vulnerabilities: 2 critical, 10 high, 5 moderate, 1 low. This change introduced none and removed none; npm audit --omit=dev reports 0, so all of them are in the build and test toolchain, which still runs on developer machines and in CI.
findings.fix: One work item fixes it for both this item and ITEM-1, so it should be raised once rather than twice: add a dependency audit to pr-checks.yml failing at an agreed severity, add a scheduled daily run so new advisories are seen without a code change, add a dependency bot to raise the upgrades, and write the time to fix per severity. The two critical findings need vitest 5.0.3, a breaking change, so they belong in that item rather than in a quick fix here.

summary: Pass, with 1 high finding open, and it is pre-existing rather than caused here: nothing audits dependencies on change or on a schedule, and 18 vulnerabilities are present (2 critical), all dev-only. The change itself adds two npm scripts, moves no version, leaves package-lock.json untouched, and ships nothing — the production bundle is byte-identical to the base's.
